### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Ullrich congenital muscular dystrophy 1B  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.793)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8948216, Reactome:R-HSA-216083, Reactome:R-HSA-3000178, Reactome:R-HSA-419037, Reactome:R-HSA-1442490)

**Proposed mechanism:** COL6A2 (HGNC:2212) —DISRUPTS→ Collagen VI Assembly and Extracellular Matrix Formation (GO:0005576); Collagen VI Assembly and Extracellular Matrix Formation (GO:0005576) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324); Collagen VI Assembly and Extracellular Matrix Formation (GO:0005576) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal muscle atrophy (HP:0003202). Mutations in COL6A2 disrupt the assembly of collagen VI, which is crucial for the structural integrity of muscle extracellular matrix. This disruption leads to downstream phenotypes of muscle weakness and skeletal muscle atrophy, common to both myosclerosis and Ullrich congenital muscular dystrophy 1B.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of a pathogenic variant in COL6A2 with a demonstrably gain-of-function effect in both diseases, or the absence of any pathogenic variants in COL6A2 in a significant cohort of patients with these conditions, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs121917932)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving COL6A2 provides a potential therapeutic target for both myosclerosis and Ullrich congenital muscular dystrophy 1B, focusing on strategies to restore collagen VI function or mitigate its downstream consequences.

#### 2. Bethlem myopathy 1B  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.783)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8948216, Reactome:R-HSA-216083, Reactome:R-HSA-3000178, Reactome:R-HSA-419037, Reactome:R-HSA-1442490)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic COL6A2 variant (HP:0003198) —DISRUPTS→ COL6A2 (HGNC:2212); COL6A2 (HGNC:2212) —DISRUPTS→ Collagen VI synthesis and assembly (GO:0031012); Collagen VI synthesis and assembly (GO:0031012) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324); Collagen VI synthesis and assembly (GO:0031012) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal muscle abnormalities (HP:0003198). Pathogenic variants in COL6A2 disrupt the synthesis and assembly of collagen VI. This leads to compromised extracellular matrix integrity in muscle tissue, manifesting as skeletal muscle abnormalities and weakness, common to both myosclerosis and Bethlem myopathy 1B.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of a pathogenic variant in COL6A2 exhibiting a gain-of-function mechanism or a completely distinct causal gene for one of the diseases would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing a pathogenic variant in COL6A2 with a frequency > 0.01% in any population.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding this shared collagen VI defect can inform therapeutic strategies targeting extracellular matrix repair or collagen VI stabilization, potentially benefiting patients with both myosclerosis and Bethlem myopathy 1B.

Mutations in COL6A1 and COL6A2 disrupt the organization of collagen VI in the extracellular matrix, leading to muscle weakness and atrophy, manifesting as myosclerosis and Ullrich congenital muscular dystrophy.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in COL6A1 or COL6A2 with a minor allele frequency >0.1% in gnomAD. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular pathology of collagen VI dysfunction in myosclerosis and Ullrich congenital muscular dystrophy 1A could inform the development of targeted therapies aimed at restoring extracellular matrix integrity or function.

#### 5. brain small vessel disease 1 with or without ocular anomalies  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.433)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8948216, Reactome:R-HSA-216083, Reactome:R-HSA-3000178, Reactome:R-HSA-419037, Reactome:R-HSA-1442490)

**Proposed mechanism:** COL4A1 (HGNC:2210) —DISRUPTS→ collagen fibril organization (GO:0030198); collagen fibril organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324); collagen fibril organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Leukoencephalopathy (HP:0002327). Loss-of-function mutations in COL4A1 disrupt the normal organization of collagen fibrils, which are critical components of both muscle tissue and the brain's small blood vessels. Impaired collagen fibril organization leads to muscle weakness (myosclerosis) and structural defects in cerebral small vessels, resulting in leukoencephalopathy characteristic of brain small vessel disease 1.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in COL4A1 with a significantly different functional impact (e.g., gain-of-function) in one of the diseases, or the absence of any COL4A1 variants in affected individuals of both cohorts. _(variant: rs115071280)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of COL4A1 in collagen fibril organization could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting connective tissue integrity that benefit patients with both myosclerosis and certain forms of small vessel disease.

#### 6. autosomal dominant Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, vascular type  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.433)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8948216, Reactome:R-HSA-216083, Reactome:R-HSA-3000178, Reactome:R-HSA-419037, Reactome:R-HSA-1442490)

**Proposed mechanism:** COL6A2 (HGNC:2210) —DISRUPTS→ collagen type VI alpha 2 chain production (GO:0030198); COL3A1 (HGNC:2207) —DISRUPTS→ collagen type III alpha 1 chain production (GO:0030198); collagen type VI alpha 2 chain production (GO:0030198) —DECREASES→ extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); collagen type III alpha 1 chain production (GO:0030198) —DECREASES→ extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324); extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Arterial dissection (HP:0005793). Mutations in COL6A2 lead to defects in collagen VI alpha 2 chain production, impacting extracellular matrix organization and contributing to muscle weakness in myosclerosis. Similarly, mutations in COL3A1 affect collagen type III alpha 1 chain production, also impairing extracellular matrix organization and leading to vascular complications such as arterial dissection in vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome. **How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in COL6A2 and COL3A1 do not affect the shared extracellular matrix organization pathway, or that genetic variants in these genes with a high frequency in gnomAD (e.g., >0.1%) are not associated with either disease. _(variant: Any common variant in COL6A2 or COL3A1)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of extracellular matrix integrity in these distinct yet mechanistically linked diseases could inform therapeutic strategies targeting matrix repair or stabilization, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.

#### 7. microangiopathy and leukoencephalopathy, pontine, autosomal dominant  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.397)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8948216, Reactome:R-HSA-216083, Reactome:R-HSA-3000178, Reactome:R-HSA-419037, Reactome:R-HSA-1442490)

Mutations in COL4A1 disrupt the proper assembly and function of Type IV Collagen, a critical component of basement membranes. This disruption leads to impaired basement membrane integrity in multiple tissues, manifesting as muscle fibrosis (myosclerosis) and vascular abnormalities including microangiopathy and leukoencephalopathy.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in COL4A1 that segregate with disease in affected families for both myosclerosis and pontine autosomal dominant microangiopathy and leukoencephalopathy would support this hypothesis. Conversely, the absence of such variants or the presence of disease-causing variants in entirely distinct pathways for both conditions would falsify it. _(variant: The presence of common, benign variants in COL4A1 in the general population (e.g., gnomAD MAF > 1%) would not falsify the hypothesis if the causative variants are rare and pathogenic.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic basis in Type IV Collagen dysfunction could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting basement membrane integrity or related pathways that could benefit patients with both myosclerosis and pontine autosomal dominant microangiopathy and leukoencephalopathy.
